(vertigo) Paroymsal Positional Vertigo.description: BPPV is an inner ear problem that causes brief episodes of vertigo (spinning sensations) when your head is moved into certain positions.
precautions: Avoid sudden or rapid head movements
Perform Epley maneuver under specialist guidance
Sleep with your head slightly elevated using extra pillows
Take care when getting out of bed in the morning
(vertigo) Paroymsal Positional Vertigo.diet_advice: Stay well hydrated and limit excessive sodium and caffeine intake.
emergency_symptoms: Loss of vision or double vision

AIDS.description: AIDS is the late stage of HIV infection that occurs when the body's immune system is badly damaged because of the virus.
precautions: Consult an infectious disease specialist immediately
Adhere strictly to prescribed Antiretroviral Therapy (ART)
Practice safe hygiene to prevent opportunistic infections
Get routine blood counts and viral load monitoring
AIDS.diet_advice: High-protein, calorie-rich balanced diet with thoroughly cooked, hygienic foods.

Acne.description: Acne is a skin condition that occurs when hair follicles become plugged with oil and dead skin cells, causing pimples, blackheads, or cysts.
precautions: Wash face twice daily with a gentle, non-comedogenic cleanser
Do not pop, squeeze, or pick at lesions to prevent scarring
Avoid touching your face with unwashed hands
Use oil-free, non-greasy skincare and sunscreen
Acne.diet_advice: Reduce refined sugars, high-glycemic foods, and dairy if triggered.
emergency_symptoms: High fever with tender skin warmth

Alcoholic hepatitis.description: Alcoholic hepatitis is inflammation of the liver caused by heavy, long-term alcohol consumption.
precautions: Cease all alcohol consumption immediately and permanently
Seek medical supervision for alcohol withdrawal and detox
Undergo liver function and ultrasound imaging tests
Rest adequately and avoid hepatotoxic medications like high-dose acetaminophen
Alcoholic hepatitis.diet_advice: Nutrient-dense, high-calorie, moderate-protein diet; monitor sodium intake if ascites is present.

Allergy.description: An allergic reaction occurs when the immune system overreacts to a harmless substance such as pollen, pet dander, or food.
precautions: Identify and eliminate exposure to suspected allergens
Keep indoor spaces ventilated and air filters clean
Wash hands and face after outdoor exposure
Carry an antihistamine or emergency epinephrine if prescribed
Allergy.diet_advice: Avoid known food allergens; drink plenty of warm fluids.
emergency_symptoms: Swelling of lips, tongue, or throat

Arthritis.description: Arthritis involves acute or chronic inflammation of one or more joints, leading to stiffness, pain, and restricted joint movement.
precautions: Engage in low-impact physical exercise such as swimming or walking
Apply alternating warm and cold compresses for pain relief
Maintain a healthy body weight to minimize joint load
Use ergonomic assistive devices during daily tasks
Arthritis.diet_advice: Anti-inflammatory diet rich in omega-3 fatty acids, turmeric, berries, and leafy greens.
emergency_symptoms: Inability to bear any weight with severe sudden joint redness and high fever (possible septic arthritis)

Bronchial Asthma.description: Asthma is a chronic respiratory condition in which the airways narrow, swell, and produce extra mucus, causing difficulty breathing.
precautions: Carry your rescue inhaler at all times
Avoid triggers such as smoke, cold air, dust mites, and strong perfumes
Monitor peak flow readings regularly
Get an annual influenza vaccination
Bronchial Asthma.diet_advice: Eat antioxidant-rich fruits and vegetables; avoid sulfites in dried fruits and processed food.
emergency_symptoms: Severe breathlessness unresponsive to rescue inhaler
Inability to speak in full sentences

Cervical spondylosis.description: Cervical spondylosis is age-related wear and tear of the spinal discs in the neck, causing neck pain, stiffness, and tingling.
precautions: Practice ergonomic posture when sitting at desks and computer screens
Perform gentle neck-stretching and strengthening exercises
Use an orthopedic cervical support pillow
Take frequent breaks from long screen sessions
Cervical spondylosis.diet_advice: Calcium and Vitamin D rich foods for bone support.
emergency_symptoms: Sudden loss of bowel or bladder control
Progressive severe arm or hand weakness

Chicken pox.description: Chickenpox is a highly contagious viral infection causing an itchy blister-like rash all over the body, along with fever.
precautions: Isolate until all blisters have crusted over completely
Apply calamine lotion to reduce itching
Keep fingernails short and clean to prevent bacterial infection
Avoid aspirin in children due to Reye's syndrome risk
Chicken pox.diet_advice: Soft, cool, bland foods if sores are inside the mouth; stay well hydrated with broths and water.
emergency_symptoms: Stiff neck, extreme drowsiness, or breathing problems

Chronic cholestasis.description: Cholestasis is a condition where bile flow from the liver is slowed or blocked, resulting in jaundice, dark urine, and severe itching.
precautions: Consult a hepatologist for liver imaging and bile acid tests
Avoid alcohol and non-essential liver-metabolized drugs
Take lukewarm rather than hot baths to ease skin itching
Supplement fat-soluble vitamins (A, D, E, K) as advised
Chronic cholestasis.diet_advice: Low-fat, easily digestible diet with medium-chain triglycerides.
emergency_symptoms: High fever with chills and severe right upper abdominal pain

Common Cold.description: The common cold is a harmless viral infection of your nose and throat, causing runny nose, sore throat, sneezing, and mild fatigue.
precautions: Get plenty of rest and sleep to support immune recovery
Drink warm fluids like herbal teas, soups, and warm water
Gargle with warm salt water for sore throat relief
Wash hands frequently and cover coughs
medications: Paracetamol or ibuprofen for body aches
Common Cold.diet_advice: Warm soups, citrus fruits rich in Vitamin C, and plenty of fluids.
emergency_symptoms: Shortness of breath or painful swallowing

Dengue.description: Dengue is a mosquito-borne viral infection causing high fever, severe retro-orbital headache, joint/bone pain, and rash.
precautions: Monitor platelet counts and hematocrit daily through blood tests
Stay aggressively hydrated with oral rehydration salts (ORS) and coconut water
Strictly avoid aspirin, ibuprofen, and NSAIDs as they increase bleeding risk
Use mosquito nets and repellents to prevent transmission
medications: Paracetamol only for fever and pain
Intravenous fluids in clinic if dehydrated
Dengue.diet_advice: Light fluids, papaya leaf extract (supportive), coconut water, pomegranate juice, and soft rice.

Diabetes.description: Diabetes is a chronic metabolic disorder characterized by elevated levels of blood glucose due to insufficient insulin production or action.
precautions: Check fasting and post-prandial blood glucose levels regularly
Engage in at least 30 minutes of moderate physical activity daily
Perform daily self-inspection of your feet for cuts or blisters
Follow your prescribed medication or insulin schedule meticulously
medications: SGLT2 inhibitors or GLP-1 receptor agonists
Diabetes.diet_advice: Low glycemic index foods, high-fiber vegetables, lean proteins; strictly minimize refined sugars and sodas.
emergency_symptoms: Extremely high blood sugar (>300 mg/dL) with fruity breath odor, nausea, or confusion (DKA)

Dimorphic hemmorhoids(piles).description: Hemorrhoids are swollen veins in your lower rectum and anus, causing itching, discomfort, and bright red rectal bleeding during bowel movements.
precautions: Avoid straining during bowel movements
Take warm sitz baths for 15-20 minutes two to three times a day
Drink at least 8 to 10 glasses of water daily
Avoid prolonged sitting on the toilet
Dimorphic hemmorhoids(piles).diet_advice: High-fiber diet including whole grains, legumes, figs, apples, and leafy greens.
emergency_symptoms: Sudden severe pain indicating a thrombosed hemorrhoid

Drug Reaction.description: An adverse drug reaction is an unexpected, unwanted, or harmful response to a medication, frequently manifesting as a widespread rash, hives, or fever.
precautions: Contact your prescribing physician immediately before stopping or changing medication
Record the name, dose, and timing of the suspected drug
Avoid re-taking the medication under any circumstance
Wear a medical alert bracelet for confirmed drug allergies
Drug Reaction.diet_advice: Drink water to aid renal clearance; light, non-irritating diet.

Fungal infection.description: Fungal skin infections (such as ringworm, athlete's foot, or jock itch) are common infections caused by fungi that thrive in warm, moist areas.
precautions: Keep affected skin areas clean, cool, and completely dry
Wear breathable, loose-fitting cotton clothing
Do not share towels, clothing, or personal hygiene items
Complete the entire course of antifungal medication even after symptoms disappear
medications: Topical clotrimazole, terbinafine, or ketoconazole cream
Oral antifungals (fluconazole, itraconazole for severe cases)
Fungal infection.diet_advice: Limit excess sugar and yeast-promoting foods; eat probiotic-rich yogurt.
emergency_symptoms: Spreading red streaks, warmth, or pus indicating secondary bacterial cellulitis

GERD.description: GERD is a chronic digestive disease in which stomach acid or bile irritates the lining of the food pipe (esophagus), causing heartburn and acid regurgitation.
precautions: Avoid lying down for at least 2 to 3 hours after eating
Elevate the head of your bed by 6 inches
Eat smaller, more frequent meals rather than large heavy dinners
Avoid triggers like fried foods, citrus, chocolate, mint, and alcohol
GERD.diet_advice: Oatmeal, non-citrus fruits (bananas, melons), lean poultry, and steamed vegetables.
emergency_symptoms: Crushing chest pain radiating to arm or jaw (mimics heart attack)

Gastroenteritis.description: Gastroenteritis is inflammation of the stomach and intestines, usually caused by viral or bacterial infection, resulting in vomiting and diarrhea.
precautions: Sip oral rehydration solution (ORS) frequently in small amounts
Follow the BRAT diet (Bananas, Rice, Applesauce, Toast) once vomiting subsides
Wash hands thoroughly after using the bathroom and before eating
Rest adequately and avoid dairy products for 48 hours
Gastroenteritis.diet_advice: Clear broths, rice water, diluted apple juice, electrolytes; avoid spicy, fatty, or caffeinated items.
emergency_symptoms: Inability to keep liquids down for 24 hours
Sunken eyes, dizziness, or dark urine (severe dehydration)

Heart attack.description: A heart attack occurs when the flow of blood to the heart is severely reduced or blocked, usually by a buildup of fat, cholesterol, and plaque in coronary arteries.
precautions: CALL EMERGENCY SERVICES (911 / 112 / 102) IMMEDIATELY
Chew an aspirin (325 mg) unless allergic or instructed otherwise
Sit upright and rest quietly while waiting for emergency responders
Do not drive yourself to the hospital
medications: Emergency thrombolytics or angioplasty in hospital
Heart attack.diet_advice: Strict cardiac care under hospital supervision.
emergency_symptoms: Pain radiating to left arm, neck, jaw, or back

Hepatitis B.description: Hepatitis B is a serious liver infection caused by the hepatitis B virus (HBV), which can become chronic and lead to liver failure, cirrhosis, or cancer.
precautions: Consult a liver specialist for viral load and liver enzyme testing
Ensure close contacts and family members receive the Hepatitis B vaccine
Avoid all alcohol and unverified herbal supplements
Practice safe sex and do not share razors, toothbrushes, or needles
Hepatitis B.diet_advice: Clean, home-cooked balanced diet rich in leafy vegetables, whole grains, and lean proteins.
emergency_symptoms: Intense yellowing of eyes and skin (deep jaundice)

Hepatitis C.description: Hepatitis C is a viral infection that causes liver inflammation, transmitted through contact with infected blood, and can lead to significant liver damage.
precautions: Undergo HCV RNA viral load and genotype testing
Direct-Acting Antivirals (DAAs) can cure over 95% of cases; complete the course
Avoid all alcohol to protect liver cells
Screen regularly for liver fibrosis or cirrhosis
Hepatitis C.diet_advice: Plant-forward, antioxidant-rich diet; low sodium if liver scarring is present.
emergency_symptoms: Vomiting blood or dark black stools

Hepatitis D.description: Hepatitis D is a liver disease caused by the hepatitis D virus (HDV), which requires the hepatitis B virus to replicate, leading to accelerated liver disease.
precautions: Specialist care at a designated liver center is essential
Strict monitoring of both HDV RNA and HBV DNA
Zero alcohol intake
Check vaccination status and family screening
Hepatitis D.diet_advice: High-nutrition, liver-protective foods; avoid excessive iron.

Hepatitis E.description: Hepatitis E is a liver disease caused by the hepatitis E virus (HEV), mainly transmitted through contaminated drinking water.
precautions: Drink only boiled or filtered purified water
Avoid raw or undercooked meats, especially pork or shellfish
CRITICAL: Pregnant women require urgent hospital monitoring as HEV carries high maternal risk
Get ample physical rest and stay hydrated
Hepatitis E.diet_advice: Easily digestible carbohydrates, boiled vegetables, light soups; avoid oily foods.

Hypertension.description: Hypertension is a common condition where the long-term force of the blood against your artery walls is high enough to cause heart disease or stroke.
precautions: Monitor blood pressure at home with a calibrated digital cuff
Reduce daily dietary sodium intake to under 1,500 - 2,000 mg
Engage in 150 minutes of moderate aerobic exercise per week
Take prescribed antihypertensive medications consistently
Hypertension.diet_advice: Adopt the DASH diet (rich in fruits, vegetables, whole grains, potassium; low in saturated fat and sodium).
emergency_symptoms: Blood pressure reading above 180/120 mmHg with severe headache, chest pain, or visual changes (hypertensive crisis)

Hyperthyroidism.description: Hyperthyroidism occurs when the thyroid gland produces too much thyroid hormone, accelerating your body's metabolism and causing weight loss and rapid heartbeat.
precautions: Consult an endocrinologist for TSH, Free T3, and Free T4 blood tests
Avoid high-iodine foods and kelp supplements
Monitor resting heart rate and avoid excessive caffeine
Protect eyes if Graves' ophthalmopathy is present
Hyperthyroidism.diet_advice: Cruciferous vegetables, calcium, Vitamin D; limit iodized salt if advised by your endocrinologist.
emergency_symptoms: Thyroid storm: high fever, extreme heart palpitations (>140 bpm), agitation or delirium

Hypoglycemia.description: Hypoglycemia is a condition characterized by abnormally low blood glucose levels (below 70 mg/dL), leading to shaking, sweating, confusion, and dizziness.
precautions: Apply the 15-15 Rule: Consume 15 grams of fast-acting carbohydrate and recheck glucose in 15 minutes
Carry glucose tablets, candies, or fruit juice at all times
Do not skip or delay scheduled meals
Review insulin or diabetes medication dosages with your doctor
Hypoglycemia.diet_advice: Complex carbohydrates paired with protein and fiber for sustained glucose release.

Hypothyroidism.description: Hypothyroidism is a condition where the thyroid gland does not produce enough thyroid hormones, leading to fatigue, weight gain, depression, and cold sensitivity.
precautions: Take prescribed levothyroxine daily on an empty stomach with a full glass of water
Wait at least 30 to 60 minutes after taking levothyroxine before eating breakfast or coffee
Get TSH blood levels monitored every 6 to 12 months
Engage in regular light exercise to boost energy and metabolism
Hypothyroidism.diet_advice: Nutritious balanced diet; moderate iodine, selenium (Brazil nuts), and zinc; avoid excessive raw goitrogens.
emergency_symptoms: Extreme hypothermia, slow heart rate, severe confusion (myxedema coma)

Impetigo.description: Impetigo is a highly contagious bacterial skin infection that causes honey-colored crusted sores, commonly around the nose and mouth.
precautions: Wash sores gently with warm antibacterial soap and water
Do not scratch or pick at crusts to prevent spreading the bacteria
Wash infected person's clothes, towels, and bed linens separately in hot water
Keep sores covered with loose gauze bandages
medications: Oral antibiotics (cephalexin, amoxicillin/clavulanate) for widespread lesions
emergency_symptoms: High fever, swollen glands, or reddish urine (post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis)

Jaundice.description: Jaundice is a yellow discoloration of the skin, sclera (whites of the eyes), and mucous membranes caused by high levels of bilirubin in the blood.
precautions: Consult a doctor promptly for comprehensive liver and biliary ultrasound testing
Completely avoid all alcohol and non-prescribed medications
Drink plenty of boiled water and clean fluids
Rest adequately and avoid strenuous physical exertion
medications: Therapy directed at underlying liver/biliary cause
Jaundice.diet_advice: Light, easily digestible carbohydrates, boiled vegetables, sugarcane juice (from hygienic sources), and fresh fruits; zero oily or fried food.
emergency_symptoms: Severe right upper quadrant pain, chills with high fever, vomiting, and mental confusion

Malaria.description: Malaria is a life-threatening disease caused by Plasmodium parasites transmitted to humans through the bites of infected female Anopheles mosquitoes.
precautions: Get a prompt rapid diagnostic test (RDT) or peripheral blood smear
Complete the full course of prescribed Artemisinin-based Combination Therapy (ACT)
Sleep under insecticide-treated bed nets
Eliminate standing water around the home where mosquitoes breed
Malaria.diet_advice: High-carbohydrate, easily digestible meals, coconut water, and soups to replenish electrolytes.
emergency_symptoms: Cerebral malaria signs: confusion, seizures, unconsciousness, severe anemia, blackish urine

Migraine.description: A migraine is a neurological condition that can cause severe throbbing pain or a pulsing sensation, usually on one side of the head, accompanied by nausea and light sensitivity.
precautions: Rest in a quiet, dark, cool room during an attack
Apply a cold cloth or ice pack to your forehead or temples
Maintain regular sleep schedules and meal times
Keep a headache diary to identify personal triggers (cheese, chocolate, stress, lights)
medications: NSAIDs or combination analgesics (aspirin, acetaminophen, caffeine)
Migraine.diet_advice: Stay well hydrated; avoid MSG, aged cheeses, artificial sweeteners, and cured meats.
emergency_symptoms: Headache with fever, stiff neck, confusion, or focal numbness

Osteoarthristis.description: Osteoarthritis is the most common form of arthritis, occurring when the protective cartilage that cushions the ends of the bones wears down over time.
precautions: Maintain an optimal body weight to reduce stress on weight-bearing joints (knees, hips)
Engage in low-impact aerobic activities like cycling and aquatic exercise
Perform quadriceps and hamstrings strengthening exercises
Use supportive footwear and walking aids if necessary
medications: Intra-articular hyaluronic acid or corticosteroid injections
Osteoarthristis.diet_advice: Mediterranean diet rich in antioxidants, olive oil, and oily fish; maintain adequate Vitamin D.
emergency_symptoms: Joint that becomes acutely hot, intensely swollen, and impossible to move with fever (septic arthritis)

Paralysis (brain hemorrhage).description: A hemorrhagic stroke occurs when a weakened blood vessel ruptures and bleeds into the surrounding brain, causing sudden paralysis and neurological impairment.
precautions: CALL EMERGENCY NUMBERS (911 / 112) IMMEDIATELY - Time is Brain!
Apply the FAST test: Face drooping, Arm weakness, Speech difficulty, Time to call
Do NOT administer aspirin or blood thinners (these worsen bleeding)
Keep the patient lying flat with head slightly elevated until medical arrival
emergency_symptoms: Sudden numbness or paralysis on one side of face/body
Sudden confusion, trouble speaking or understanding

Peptic ulcer diseae.description: Peptic ulcers are painful open sores that develop on the inside lining of your stomach and the upper portion of your small intestine, often due to H. pylori or NSAIDs.
precautions: Get tested for Helicobacter pylori bacteria
Avoid NSAIDs like ibuprofen, aspirin, and naproxen
Limit consumption of spicy, acidic foods and caffeinated beverages
Quit smoking and avoid all alcohol
Peptic ulcer diseae.diet_advice: Probiotic foods (kefir, yogurt), broccoli, apples, cabbage; avoid midnight snacking.

Pneumonia.description: Pneumonia is an infection that inflames the air sacs in one or both lungs, which may fill with fluid or pus, causing cough with phlegm, fever, chills, and breathing trouble.
precautions: Seek medical evaluation and chest X-ray without delay
Take prescribed antibiotics or antivirals exactly as instructed until finished
Monitor blood oxygen saturation with a pulse oximeter (keep above 94%)
Rest thoroughly and drink plenty of warm fluids
Pneumonia.diet_advice: Protein-rich soups, warm broths, ginger tea; avoid chilled drinks and dairy if it thickens phlegm.

Psoriasis.description: Psoriasis is a chronic autoimmune skin disease that causes rapid buildup of skin cells, forming scales and itchy, dry red patches.
precautions: Keep skin moisturized daily with thick ointments or creams
Avoid skin injuries, cuts, sunburns, or scratching (Koebner phenomenon)
Manage stress through mindfulness and gentle exercise
Take lukewarm baths with colloidal oatmeal or bath oils
medications: Biologics or oral immunosuppressants for moderate-severe cases
Psoriasis.diet_advice: Anti-inflammatory diet rich in omega-3 fatty acids, flaxseeds, and leafy greens; reduce alcohol and red meat.
emergency_symptoms: Erythrodermic psoriasis: widespread redness covering more than 80% of body with shivering or fever

Tuberculosis.description: Tuberculosis is a potentially serious infectious disease that mainly affects the lungs, caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis bacteria.
precautions: Adhere strictly to the full 6-to-9 month course of Directly Observed Treatment (DOTS)
Wear a mask and stay in well-ventilated rooms during initial infectious phase
Never skip doses to prevent Multi-Drug Resistant TB (MDR-TB)
Ensure close household contacts are tested
Tuberculosis.diet_advice: High-protein, energy-dense meals (eggs, milk, pulses, nuts) to regain lost body weight.
emergency_symptoms: Coughing up significant amounts of bright red blood (hemoptysis)

Typhoid.description: Typhoid fever is a life-threatening bacterial infection caused by Salmonella typhi, usually spread through contaminated food or water.
precautions: Obtain blood culture or Widal test for definitive diagnosis
Drink only boiled, bottled, or chemically disinfected water
Complete the entire antibiotic regimen prescribed by your doctor
Wash hands thoroughly with soap after using the toilet
Typhoid.diet_advice: Bland, easily digestible foods like porridge, boiled potatoes, soft rice, and banana; avoid high-fiber raw vegetables and fried foods.
emergency_symptoms: Severe persistent abdominal pain, rigid tender abdomen (risk of bowel perforation)

Urinary tract infection.description: A UTI is an infection in any part of the urinary system (kidneys, ureters, bladder, and urethra), most commonly involving the lower urinary tract.
precautions: Drink plenty of water to help flush bacteria from your urinary tract
Wipe from front to back after urinating or bowel movements
Urinate promptly after sexual intercourse
Do not hold urine for extended periods
Urinary tract infection.diet_advice: Pure unsweetened cranberry juice, high water intake; avoid bladder irritants like coffee, alcohol, and spicy foods.
emergency_symptoms: High fever with chills and severe lower back / flank pain (indicates kidney infection - pyelonephritis)

Varicose veins.description: Varicose veins are swollen, twisted veins that lie just under the surface of the skin, most commonly in the legs, caused by weakened vein valves.
precautions: Wear graduated compression stockings during daily activities
Elevate your legs above heart level for 15 minutes three times daily
Avoid standing or sitting in one position for long stretches
Maintain a healthy body weight and engage in daily walking
medications: Endovenous laser ablation or sclerotherapy for advanced cases
Varicose veins.diet_advice: High-fiber foods to prevent constipation (which raises venous pressure); rutin-rich foods like buckwheat and citrus.
emergency_symptoms: Sudden severe redness, pain, and swelling in one leg (risk of deep vein thrombosis)
Bleeding from a ruptured varicose vein

hepatitis A.description: Hepatitis A is a highly contagious, short-term liver infection caused by the hepatitis A virus (HAV), predominantly spread through contaminated food or water.
precautions: Practice meticulous hand hygiene with soap and running water
Drink only boiled, safe drinking water and avoid street food
Rest thoroughly as fatigue can persist for several weeks
Avoid all alcohol and hepatotoxic medications during recovery
hepatitis A.diet_advice: Small, frequent carbohydrate-rich meals; fruit juices, boiled vegetables, and soups; avoid all fatty or greasy meals.
emergency_symptoms: Inability to retain liquids, extreme dizziness, dark cola-colored urine, or severe confusion
